title: First lodgings and impressions of New York
summary: He roomed on 129th Street for eight dollars a week and says New York lived up to what he was told.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So these drummers were all in New York at the time. Where did you stay in New York when you first got to New York?
I stayed at a place on 129th Street, a private house. I was paying about eight dollars a week for a room. I had a few dollars when I came here.
You had your drums set up in the room?
Well, I had them in the case.
In the case, mmm-hmm. Did you...?
In a box. I had them in a box, with a lock on the box.
Did you get a chance to practice them? Was it necessary to practice...?
No, it wasn't necessary. I was young and very fly.
I was... I don't think I knew too much about drums, how to play 'em, when to play 'em...
Was New York... As you think back on it, was New York... Did it measure up to what you expected or what people told you about it?
